correctness.rationale: Double transitivity gives an irreducible degree-(n-1) standard constituent with character equal to fixed-points minus one. Schur orthogonality identifies its central convolution kernel. Endpoint convolution norms equal kernel ell-1 mass; the character is negative exactly on derangements, where it equals -1, and has total sum zero, yielding absolute mass 2D. The complementary kernel is computed exactly. Cameron-Cohen supplies D>=|G|/n with the Frobenius equality case, and orbit-stabilizer gives |G|>=n(n-1), proving the sharp contractivity classification. The bundled verifier checks representative finite cases exactly but is not part of the universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies a canonical nonabelian Fourier-block endpoint norm with derangement density for every finite doubly transitive action and turns norm-one complementarity into an exact characterization of sharp double transitivity, with the complement becoming Haar averaging on the Frobenius kernel. This is a natural structural boundary theorem rather than a fixed-size computation or arbitrary slice.
